column1: # The trees this port borrows from. One `name<space>path` per line; `~` is home.
# SAFARI DOES NOT PIN THE LANGUAGE. It used to: a `cobblestone` line here named
# safari's own Cobblestone worktree, a SECOND copy of a pin the transpilers
# already carry -- and the copy that drifts. On 2026-09-09 it sat at 422405d0
# (Update 55 era) while both transpilers had moved to 8570fba1 (the Update 58
# candidate), so the arms would have graded a U55 language with U57 binaries and
# nothing said so. The whole private-pin mechanism dated to the earliest days
# and was never anything but a footgun.
# THE LANGUAGE IS NOW DERIVED FROM THE BORROWED BINARIES. codexzig and codexwasm
# each record the checkout they were built from in their generated provenance;
# `harness/cobblestone_pin.py` reads both, REFUSES if they disagree, and hands
# back the path. The agreement of the two transpilers IS the drift check, at the
# one place it matters, and there is no safari copy left to fall out of step.
# `SAFARI_COBBLESTONE` still overrides explicitly for a candidate build.
# WHAT STAYS HERE is only the two things safari borrows: the transpiler trees.
# This project BUILDS NEITHER. Each exists to be a fixed point -- the emitter
# emitting the same bytes for its own source on two roads -- which is a stronger
# claim about a binary than this project could make about one it assembled. So
# safari PULLS EXECUTABLES; `harness/build_codex{zig,wasm}.sh` fingerprint the
# binary against its tree's own generated source and refuse a mismatch, and
# every run's PROVENANCE records the path and size of what actually ran.
# `CODEXZIG=`/`CODEXWASM=` override for a candidate build -- that is what they
# are for, and NOT a way to make a stale pin look current.
# THE PATH IS THE PIN AND THE COMMIT IS NOT: each tree is one nobody else moves,
# so what it holds is checkable with `git -C <path> log -1`.
# UPSTREAM NOW REGISTERS `Safari`, `Judge` AND `Gold` ITSELF. Update 55 took this
# port into the depot as apps/safari/port. Both bundlers give the names below the
# last word -- they mean THIS project's directories -- and both say so on every
# bundle rather than resolving somewhere else in silence.
codexzig    ~/showell_repos/codex-zig-transpiler
codexwasm   ~/showell_repos/codex-wasm-transpiler
